Elena — thanks for the clear ask and for the attachments. Short answers up front:

- Redwood treats major cloud providers (IaaS/PaaS) as subservice organizations using the carve-out method in our SOC 2 report. Our SOC 2 Type II references the cloud provider's own SOC report for controls in scope that are their responsibility.

- We can provide a bridge letter covering the audit window you specified, and we will explicitly call out shared responsibilities (networking, hypervisor, physical security, and basic infra patching) vs. Redwood responsibilities (application-level controls, access control in our platform, encryption at rest/in-transit where we manage keys).

To proceed we'll need:
- Your preferred bridge-letter recipient name and any legal language BluePeak requires.
- Confirmation of the audit period (you listed 2026-02-01 to 2026-04-30).
- Any specific controls or control IDs your customer is focused on (e.g., logging retention, KMS/HSM ownership, SOC control IDs).

We can share a draft bridge letter and a subservice mapping spreadsheet that shows for each control who is responsible: BluePeak, Redwood, or Shared. Mina will own the draft bridge letter; Vivek, I've CC'd you to surface any contractual constraints (procurement/PO language).

I'll put together the draft by COB Wed (23 Mar).
